issues.summary: Words matter. When you sit down to write a brand guidelines document, you are not just picking colors or fonts. You are creating a foundational grammar and terminology playbook for your entire organization. If your creative team confuses the terms “brand,” “branding,” and “identity,” they will inevitably produce inconsistent copy. Inconsistent copy confuses readers, dilutes The post How Do You Cra
issues.author: Daily Writing Tips
issues.content_html:
Words matter. When you sit down to write a brand guidelines document, you are not just picking colors or fonts. You are creating a foundational grammar and terminology playbook for your entire organization. If your creative team confuses the terms “brand,” “branding,” and “identity,” they will inevitably produce inconsistent copy. Inconsistent copy confuses readers, dilutes your core message, and makes your business appear unprofessional.

The primary goal of this guide is to clarify these specific terms for writers. By establishing clear terminology definitions, your internal documentation will set a precise standard for every single piece of content you publish. When your copywriters, editors, and marketers speak the same language, the resulting content becomes sharp, unified, and highly effective.

What is the Grammatical Difference Between Brand, Branding, and Identity?

Words function differently based on their part of speech. Understanding the grammatical function of these three core words helps creative teams use them correctly in strategy meetings, content briefs, and final documentation. When your writers know the exact definition and grammatical role of each term, they communicate with precision. They stop using the words interchangeably, which immediately elevates the quality of your internal and external communications.

How Should You Define “Brand” in Your Terminology Guide?

“Brand” is a noun. It is the abstract concept or the emotional relationship a customer has with a company. You cannot hold a brand in your hands. It is the gut feeling a person gets when they hear your company name.

In your style guide, instruct writers to treat the brand as the core subject of your business narrative. A professional brand design firm helps establish this foundation by mapping out the psychological landscape of the business. However, your writers must maintain that foundation through consistent and careful noun usage. Provide clear examples in your documentation of how to write about the brand accurately. For instance, instruct writers to say “Our brand represents trust” rather than “Our branding is trust.”

Why Does “Branding” Require Active Verbs?

“Branding” functions as an active verb or a gerund. It represents the ongoing actions, campaigns, and communications a company executes to shape its reputation in the market. Branding is an active, never-ending process.

Instruct your writers to use active voice and strong action verbs when describing branding efforts in their internal documentation. Branding is never passive. It is the daily process of writing, designing, communicating, and publishing. In your guidelines document, emphasize that branding requires verbs like “building,” “executing,” “launching,” and “communicating.” This grammatical distinction reminds the team that branding is something they actively do every single day.

What Nouns and Adjectives Best Describe “Identity”?

“Identity” is a noun that encompasses a collection of tangible assets. While the “brand” is an abstract feeling, the “identity” is what you can see, hear, and read. This includes your logos, your typography choices, and your specific vocabulary lists.

Give your writers actionable tips on curating a list of approved adjectives that describe the brand identity accurately. Are you “bold and energetic” or “calm and professional”? Defining these specific adjectives in your guidelines leaves no room for grammatical guesswork. When writers have a concrete list of approved adjectives, they can easily craft copy that matches the visual identity perfectly.

How Do You Establish Grammar and Tone Rules in Your Guidelines?

Once you have defined your core terminology, you must pivot to the practical application of these definitions. Creating the “Voice and Tone” section of a brand guidelines document requires laying down specific, unbreakable rules for your writers.

Here are the key elements you need to include:

  • Punctuation Choices: Establish clear rules for punctuation. Specify whether your company uses the Oxford comma. State your rules on exclamation points, semicolons, and parentheses. Clear punctuation rules prevent stylistic clashes when multiple writers work on the same project.
  • Banned Words: Create a comprehensive list of banned words that dilute your message. These might include industry jargon, overly complex vocabulary, or weak modifiers like “very” and “really.”
  • Sentence Structure Preferences: Outline your preferred sentence structures. If your brand voice is punchy and modern, instruct writers to favor short, active sentences. If your voice is more academic, provide guidelines on structuring longer, more complex sentences without losing the reader’s attention.

How Can Your Creative Team Implement This Document?

A guidelines document is only useful if people actually read it and apply it. You need a structured plan to ensure your creative team adopts these new rules.

Here is a short checklist for rolling out your new terminology guide:

  • Host a Dedicated Training Session: Do not just email the document. Schedule a meeting focused strictly on terminology and grammar to walk the team through the new standards.
  • Update Onboarding Materials: Make the brand guidelines document the very first thing new copywriters read during their onboarding process.
  • Equip Your Editors: Require your editing team to use the guide as a daily reference checklist during the proofreading stage. If a piece of copy violates the established grammar rules, the editor must send it back for revisions.
  • Schedule Quarterly Reviews: Language evolves, and your guidelines should too. Review the document every few months to add new vocabulary words or clarify confusing grammar rules.

How Do We Conclude This Guide?

Creating a successful brand guidelines document ultimately relies on strict terminology and absolute grammatical clarity. If your creative team does not understand the fundamental difference between abstract concepts and actionable processes, your external messaging will suffer.

To recap the most important points from this guide, you must define “brand” as an abstract noun representing customer relationships. You must define “branding” as the active, ongoing process of shaping that reputation. Finally, you must define “identity” as the tangible, physical assets and specific vocabulary that represent your company to the world.

Take the time to audit your current style guides today. Ensure your grammar rules are clear and your terminology is strictly defined. For more practical business writing advice, grammar rules, and copywriting strategies, subscribe to the dailywritingtips.com newsletter today.

issues.title: How Do You Write Formal Email Sign-Offs That Leave a Lasting Impression?
issues.summary: Crafting a digital message takes effort, and most people focus all their energy on the subject line and the main body. They meticulously choose their opening hook and structure their arguments to sound persuasive. Yet, right at the very end, they drop the ball. The closing of your message is the final thing the recipient The post How Do You Write Formal Email Sign-Offs That Leave a Lasting Impress
issues.author: Daily Writing Tips
issues.content_html:
Crafting a digital message takes effort, and most people focus all their energy on the subject line and the main body. They meticulously choose their opening hook and structure their arguments to sound persuasive. Yet, right at the very end, they drop the ball. The closing of your message is the final thing the recipient reads, and it leaves a lingering taste.

A strong email closing is just as important as a good subject line. Proper grammar, precise capitalization, and correct punctuation in an email sign-off leave a polished and highly competent impression. If you fail to stick the landing, your entire message might feel sloppy or rushed. Learning how to properly conclude your messages is a vital skill for anyone looking to build strong business relationships.

Why Is a Proper Sign-Off Crucial for Your Professional Correspondence?

A well-crafted closing carries significant psychological and professional impact. It acts as the final handshake in a virtual environment. When you communicate in the workplace, every single detail contributes to your personal brand and credibility. Crafting a high-quality, professional email establishes a firm standard for corporate communication.

Establishing the Tone of the Relationship

The sign-off dictates the tone of the relationship moving forward. In a world where inboxes are flooded daily, taking the time to format a polite and grammatically flawless goodbye makes you stand out as a careful and considerate professional. Your choice of words reveals exactly how you perceive your professional dynamic:

  • Overly casual closings: These risk appearing disrespectful to new clients or senior leadership.
  • Highly archaic closings: These can make you seem cold or unapproachable to a close colleague.
  • Properly balanced closings: These demonstrate a high attention to detail and respect for the person on the receiving end of the screen.

What Are the Strict Grammar and Punctuation Rules for Email Closings?

Many professionals rely on autocorrect or simply copy what they see others doing, which leads to widespread grammatical errors in email sign-offs. There are strict rules governing how you format the end of your message.

Mastering the Sentence Case Rule

The first major rule concerns capitalization. In standard English writing, only the first word of a sign-off phrase should be capitalized. This rule is called sentence case, and it applies universally to email closings. For example, you must write “Best regards,” with a lowercase “r.” Writing “Best Regards,” with a capital “r” is a grammatical error. You treat the sign-off as a single, continuous phrase where only the initial letter of the very first word earns capitalization.

Applying the Terminal Comma

The second critical rule involves punctuation. You must place a terminal comma immediately after the sign-off phrase and before your name. This comma serves as a natural pause, signaling that your name is about to follow. Omitting this comma creates a run-on effect that looks highly unprofessional. Your signature block should always follow a clear vertical structure consisting of the sign-off phrase, the comma, a line break, and then your name.

Which Formal Email Sign-Offs Are Best for Different Contexts?

Selecting the right closing phrase depends entirely on the context of your conversation. You need to read the room and adjust your language based on the recipient and the nature of the correspondence.

When Should You Use Traditional Closings Like “Sincerely” or “Yours Faithfully”?

Traditional closings carry a sense of formality and historical weight. You should rely on these phrases when writing to highly formal institutions, legal entities, or government officials. They are safe, reliable choices when you are applying for a job or reaching out to a corporate executive for the first time.

Here are the most common traditional closings and their appropriate contexts:

  • Yours faithfully: This is a standard convention in British English when the email begins with a generic greeting like “Dear Sir/Madam.”
  • Sincerely: American English relies heavily on this closing for both known and unknown recipients in formal settings.
  • Respectfully: This is best used when addressing government officials, military personnel, or high-ranking executives.

How Do You Navigate Modern Business Closings Like “Best Regards” or “Kind Regards”?

For most day-to-day corporate emails, traditional closings can feel far too stiff. Modern business environments favor a careful balance of professionalism and warmth. These sign-offs are incredibly versatile and work well when communicating with vendors, active clients, or colleagues in different departments.

Consider these modern standards for your daily correspondence:

  • Best regards: This remains the absolute gold standard for daily corporate emails.
  • Kind regards: This offers a slightly more formal tone while remaining highly versatile.
  • Warm regards: This phrase is completely acceptable if you want to convey a friendlier, more approachable tone.

What Are the Common Grammatical Mistakes to Avoid in Sign-Offs?

Even seasoned professionals make frequent errors at the end of their emails. You must avoid these specific pitfalls to maintain a polished image. Always spell out your words completely to maintain a dignified tone.

  1. Over-capitalization: Writing “Warm Regards,” violates standard sentence case rules.
  2. Omitting the terminal comma: Writing “Best regards” followed immediately by your name on the next line is incorrect punctuation.
  3. Using informal abbreviations: Signing off with “Thx,” “Rgds,” or “Cheers” is highly inappropriate for formal business communications because it suggests you are too rushed to type a full word.

How Can You Summarize Your Professional Email Sign-Off Strategy?

Your sign-off is the final opportunity to reinforce your competence and professionalism before the recipient closes the window. By applying strict grammar rules and carefully matching your tone to the situation, you guarantee that your digital correspondence creates a lasting and positive impression. The correct tone combined with flawless execution shows that you are a serious professional who respects both your own brand and your recipient’s time.

Remember the core highlights of email closing etiquette. You must only capitalize the first letter of the sign-off phrase, and you must always use a comma immediately before your name. Whether you choose the traditional weight of a phrase like “Sincerely,” or the modern warmth of “Best regards,” adhering to these structural rules ensures your message is always well-received.

Do you want to master every aspect of professional writing? Subscribe to the dailywritingtips.com newsletter today for more in-depth grammar guides, vocabulary lessons, and communication strategies delivered straight to your inbox. Share this article with your colleagues and network to help improve workplace communication and ensure everyone on your team leaves a brilliant impression in every single email they send.

issues.title: The Learning-Visibility Loop: How AI Should Participate in Education
issues.summary: Generic AI is built to hand over answers. The bigger opportunity in education is to make the learning itself visible, for students and for the instructors teaching them. A finished assignment doesn’t show how it was made. It shows what a student turned in, but not how they read the prompt, where they got stuck, […] The post The Learning-Visibility Loop: How AI Should Participate in Education appea
issues.author: Grammarly
issues.content_html:
Generic AI is built to hand over answers. The bigger opportunity in education is to make the learning itself visible, for students and for the instructors teaching them.

A finished assignment doesn’t show how it was made. It shows what a student turned in, but not how they read the prompt, where they got stuck, which misconceptions surfaced, or what finally helped them move forward. Those moments are where learning actually happens, and they disappear the moment the work is submitted.

AI has widened that gap. The process is even harder to see now, and students, reaching for whatever tool is closest, get generic help that was never built for learning. Retention, integrity, and faculty workload were already compounding pressures on academic leaders. AI is adding to the pressure.

Why AI in higher education makes learning harder to see clearly

The instinct for many in education is to ask whether students used AI. We think the more useful question is, “Can educators tell that students are learning?” Visibility has become a greater challenge since the introduction of AI in education; instructors see the final submission but not the work that led up to it. The learning process itself has become opaque, even to the people responsible for teaching it.

A loop that makes learning visible

There’s a better way to work when AI is in the mix, one that turns that lost process back into something an instructor can see and act on. We call it the learning-visibility loop. Each turn of a student’s work informs the instructor’s next move, and each move shapes stronger work, so every round leaves both sides further along than the last. Here’s how it comes together.

A student works through a problem with an AI agent, a tool that holds a back-and-forth and works alongside them, guiding them rather than handing over the answer. That interaction leaves an honest record of how the student got there. The instructor reads that record, sees where the class is getting stuck, and shapes the next assignment around it. The student works again, now on ground the last round helped shape.

Each turn feeds the next. Instead of ending with a single graded assignment, every round gives an instructor something to act on, and every new assignment is shaped by what students actually struggled with. The loop moves teaching from what happened to what to do next.

One design choice holds the whole thing together: The agent guides the student rather than generating the work. An agent that hands over answers leaves no record of how the student got there. An agent that asks questions and pushes for revision creates that record, because the back-and-forth is itself the trace of how the student worked through the problem. That is what makes the help genuinely educational, and it keeps the instructor’s signal honest. The two sides are one system, and each makes the other stronger.

What faculty told us

The loop is informed by first-party research led by Yolanda Wiggins, a senior researcher at Superhuman: 12 in-depth interviews with US higher education professionals, from professors and adjuncts to academic and technology leaders. The findings are qualitative and directional. The student side draws on separate, prior research with students.

Two things came through clearly.

1. Faculty want to see how learning happens

Again and again, instructors said they wanted to understand where students were struggling and what they could do differently as teachers.

“We have no idea what prompts they used. Most of this is very opaque to me.” — a CIO who also teaches graduate courses

“We need to know what’s in their heads, not what AI can write.” — an MBA program director

“You’re gonna have to give me all of your prompts, and show me the dialogue.” — a social-psychology professor

Some instructors are already rebuilding this visibility by hand, redesigning assignments at real cost to their time. That effort is the clearest sign of the gap.

2. Students want to show their work

This second finding comes from separate, prior qualitative research with undergraduate and graduate students, who documented their real coursework and tool use. Students reached for AI when they were stuck, to interpret a prompt, get started, or check their work, not to do the assignment for them, and they valued tools that supported their thinking while keeping the work their own. Many are already opting into Grammarly Authorship, which documents how a piece of writing actually came together. The desire for greater visibility runs in both directions.

“You can’t just outsource your homework to AI. You can tell, it just creates AI slop. When students instead use it as a tutor or study buddy, we see much better work.” — an MIS professor

What keeps the loop honest

The loop only works if a few things stay true.

First, humans do the work and own the decisions. Students remain the authors of their own learning, so the agent guides while the thinking and the work stay theirs. Instructors stay the decision-makers, so insight informs a teaching decision without ever making one. As one MBA program director put it, “I will never use AI to grade.” We design for exactly that: the instructor stays the decision-maker, and the tools inform decisions rather than make them.

Second, the student-side agent must be built to support learning. When it’s built well, it does four things:

Third, the instructor-side report has to lead with what to do next. It answers three questions a busy instructor rarely has time to answer alone:

The point is to turn otherwise invisible patterns into a teaching decision, while grading, intervention, and course design remain firmly in human hands. Imagine a report that shows most of the class opened with a one-sided thesis, and that once the agent pushed back, the majority revised toward a stronger argument while a smaller group stayed stuck. That gap is the signal, and it points to exactly what to teach next.

What the loop collects, and what it leaves alone

Because the loop is based on how students learn, it collects only what helps teaching: the work process and class-level patterns, not personal or non-academic data. Students should know what’s captured, see what’s inferred, and be able to contest it. And the institution should stay in control of its own data.

Why higher education needs AI built for learning

Generic AI is getting very good at generating answers. Education needs something different: learning support that leaves an instructor with something to teach. That’s a fundamentally different product problem, and general-purpose assistants weren’t designed to solve it.

This is what it looks like when AI is built for education rather than pointed at it. It keeps students doing the doing, gives faculty a path forward instead of more to police, and gives institutions something they can actually measure: whether learning is happening. It complements an institution’s approach to AI rather than competing with it. And it’s built the way the best campus AI is being built right now: with institutions, not just for them.

Keeping learning visible

When an answer is always a click away, the work worth protecting is the learning. The learning-visibility loop is how we think AI can protect it: by keeping students in the work, keeping instructors in the decisions, and making the learning itself visible to both.

Grammarly is now part of Superhuman , and this is the model we’re building toward with Superhuman Go , alongside the institutions putting it into practice. The best campus AI isn’t handed down from a vendor; it’s shaped by the educators who know what learning should look like and built on a foundation higher ed already trusts.

issues.author: Grammarly
issues.content_html:
Instructors want to trust the work students hand in. Students want credit for the work they actually did. As AI use in the classroom becomes routine, both are getting harder, and that’s exactly where writing transparency earns its place.

Grammarly Authorship was built to close that gap.

Since Grammarly Authorship launched in beta in Google Docs in October 2024, it has expanded to Grammarly Docs, Microsoft Word, and Word Online, so students can show their writing process wherever they write. It now recognizes AI-generated content both pasted in and generated from within a document, including Copilot in Word and Gemini in Google Docs.

Students have generated more than 5 million Authorship reports to date.

The results show up on campus. After introducing Authorship across its English department, Rowan-Cabarrus Community College reduced academic integrity violations from 27 to 1, a 96% drop, in a single semester.

Authorship delivers value on its own. It goes further when it’s built into the systems an institution already runs. After integrating with Canvas LMS in September 2025, Grammarly Authorship now integrates with Blackboard, giving institutions a scalable way to make student writing transparent while students keep writing in the tools they prefer to use.

What is Grammarly Authorship?

Grammarly Authorship automatically categorizes the sources of text in a document, whether it’s in Google Docs, Microsoft Word, Word Online, or Grammarly Docs. It gives quick signals and detailed reports showing where writing came from: human-typed, AI-generated, copied, or rephrased with Grammarly’s generative AI.

Unlike traditional detection tools, Authorship is built on transparency and attribution, with student consent. Students can show their authentic writing process, and instructors can spend their time guiding rather than second-guessing it with unclear data.

Authorship’s new Blackboard integration

Instructors can require Authorship reports directly within Blackboard assignments. Here’s how it works:

1. Instructor setup

While creating an assignment, instructors simply switch on the new Enable Grammarly Authorship option in the Originality Report section of their Blackboard assignment settings.

2. Students keep writing where they always do

In the tools they already use (Microsoft Word, Word Online, Google Docs, or Grammarly Docs), students can turn on Authorship tracking with a single click and view their Authorship report at any time. It attributes their text sources automatically when they use a gen AI tool or paste from a third-party source. Because Authorship is student-first, students can see their own writing process data but can’t alter it before sharing, which builds two-way visibility into how the work was made.

3. Sharing to Blackboard is easy with a share link

When they’re ready to submit, students select Anyone with the link in their Authorship report access settings.

4. Quick attachment through normal submission workflow

Students attach the Authorship report to their normal Blackboard submission by submitting their report’s share link alongside their assignment document.

5. Instructor insights at scale

Instructors gain a class-level view of the Authorship report and can open any individual student’s full writing process replay when they want to dig in. That makes it easy to focus on outliers while trusting that every submission includes transparent attribution.

Why this matters

Educators want writing to be something students genuinely work through, and institutions need a way to trust in that work as AI use becomes routine. Students want that too: Many are actively looking for ways to use AI they can stand behind .

Here’s what the Blackboard integration gives each group:

  • Students get a low-effort way to show their writing process and get credit for their own thinking, whether or not they used AI, plus protection from false accusations. Over time, attributing their sources builds the AI-literacy habits that matter well beyond any single assignment.
  • I nstructors get assignment-level control with the ability to require students to submit an Authorship report with their assignment. Authorship is visible in Blackboard through a single class view, meaning instructors don’t have to open reports one by one. It also allows them to drill into any student’s process when a conversation is warranted. That gives back hours during grading and turns integrity checks into teaching moments rather than investigations.
  • Institutions get a consistent, scalable way to maintain academic trust across departments, built on tools faculty and students already use, so adoption doesn’t hinge on changing anyone’s habits, plus a defensible answer when leadership asks how AI is being handled.

The Blackboard Authorship integration is now available for Grammarly for Education customers on any institution-wide plan that uses Blackboard. Administrators can install the LTI in a few steps using the setup guide .

We’re glad to partner with Anthology and our school and university customers to make writing transparency a reality for the AI era.

To learn more or get started, visit Grammarly for Education .

issues.content_html:
Writing on your phone is still, somehow, a chore. Between a cramped keyboard, autocorrect that guesses wrong, and the mental load of trying to stay focused while on the move, sending a polished message takes longer than it should.

Voice dictation promised to fix this. But native phone dictation just gives you a raw transcript, full of filler words, false starts, and missing punctuation. Cleaning up your text is just as much work as if you’d typed it manually.

That’s what speech-to-text in the Grammarly Keyboard is built to solve. The Grammarly’ Keyboard now lets you dictate directly into any app and delivers clean, polished text without the cleanup.

Dictate anywhere, get polished text.

Speech-to-text is built directly into the Grammarly Keyboard. Tap the mic icon, speak naturally, and Grammarly returns clean, send-ready text—right in the app you’re using.

Grammarly’s speech-to-text handles a wide range of languages, accents, and speaking cadences. Instead of producing a raw transcript, Grammarly cuts filler words, removes spots where you corrected yourself verbally, and fixes grammar, all while preserving your tone and intent.

If you want to take your dictated text further, Grammarly’s AI assistant is available in the same keyboard. You can switch between speaking and typing at any point, or edit your dictated text with the same Grammarly Keyboard across all your apps.

Built for wherever and however you use your phone

Grammarly’s speech-to-text is for anyone who writes a lot on mobile—knowledge workers drafting between meetings, students capturing ideas mid-walk, or anyone tired of fighting a tiny keyboard.

Grammarly’s mic is designed to cut background noise while also keeping you in control of what is recorded. The mic only activates when you tap it. While it’s on, you’ll see a clear signal in the keyboard, plus the iOS orange indicator light at the top of your screen. After your audio is processed into text, it’s deleted. It isn’t stored, linked to your account, or used to train any models. All that’s left is your polished message, ready to send.

Get started

Speech-to-text lives inside the Grammarly Keyboard. Once it’s set as your default keyboard, the mic is available in any app.

  • Download and install Grammarly for iOS : If you haven’t done so already, download the Grammarly Keyboard from the App Store. Setup takes under a minute.
  • Set Grammarly as your keyboard: Go to Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards → Add New Keyboard, then select Grammarly. Enable full access when prompted. This allows the keyboard to work across all your apps.
  • Tap the mic and start speaking: Open any app, tap into a text field, and you’ll see the Grammarly Keyboard. Hit the mic icon, say what you want to write, then stop. Clean, ready-to-send text appears right where your cursor is.

issues.title: A University of Florida Professor Stopped Fighting AI in His Classroom: A Peer-Reviewed Study Followed
issues.summary: When Dr. Brian Harfe first noticed that AI tools could answer his essay prompts better than most of his students, he did not panic. He redesigned the assignment. That decision, made in a large-enrollment course at the University of Florida, has since become the subject of a peer-reviewed study published in TechTrends in 2026. What […] The post A University of Florida Professor Stopped Fighting AI
issues.author: Grammarly
issues.content_html:
When Dr. Brian Harfe first noticed that AI tools could answer his essay prompts better than most of his students, he did not panic. He redesigned the assignment.

That decision, made in a large-enrollment course at the University of Florida, has since become the subject of a peer-reviewed study published in TechTrends in 2026. What started as one professor’s practical response to a fast-moving problem is now a data-backed framework for how institutions can approach AI in student writing.

The problem with how we have been measuring AI use

Most institutions trying to get a handle on student AI use have landed on two approaches: surveys and AI detectors. Both fall short in predictable ways.

Self-reported survey data is shaped by what students think their instructors want to hear. Students who see AI use as acceptable tend to over-report it; those who fear academic penalties tend to under-report it. Even honest responses run into a memory problem. Few students can accurately reconstruct how much of a final draft came from a chatbot versus their own editing across multiple writing sessions.

AI detectors have a different problem. They work probabilistically, assessing whether text is likely to be AI-generated rather than confirming whether it actually is. None currently achieve 100% accuracy, and most do not tell you how much of a document is AI-generated or which parts. Just a verdict on the whole, which treats writing as a product rather than a process.

Institutions are left with plenty of anxiety about student AI use and very little reliable data about what students are actually doing.

A different approach to the assignment itself

Dr. Harfe’s response was not to add surveillance. It was to change what the assignment asked students to do.

In his University of Florida course titled “Can We Design Better Humans? Should We?”, he redesigned the final essay around AI rather than removing it. Students were required to begin with a fully AI-generated draft, then revise it to reflect their own views on human cloning and genetic engineering. The final submission had to represent the student’s perspective. How much of the AI draft they kept, changed, or discarded was up to them.

That design did something the traditional essay could not: It removed the incentive to hide AI use. Students were not penalized for leaning on the draft or rewarded for avoiding it. The question shifted from whether they used AI to what they actually did with it.

To track that objectively, Dr. Harfe used Grammarly Authorship, a writing transparency tool that tracks the origin of text. Unlike AI detectors, Authorship does not deal in probability. It records provenance, identifying whether each word was typed by a human, copied from an AI tool, or pulled from another source.

Students submitted their Authorship reports alongside their essays, and Dr. Harfe could use the tool’s replay feature to watch how each submission evolved from AI draft to finished product.

What 310 essays revealed

The resulting dataset, 310 essays from students across seven colleges and more than 100 declared majors, is the foundation of the study, Quantitative Analysis of Generative AI Text Usage and Identification of Factors Influencing Text Choice, that Harfe co-authored with Aaron Thomas of the University of Florida’s Information Technology department. It is among the first studies to track student AI use at the word level across a large, diverse undergraduate cohort.

Three findings stand out.

  1. Engagement shows up in the data. Students who wrote more of their own text took significantly longer to complete the assignment. The correlation was strong and consistent. Time-on-task tracked closely with how much students actually revised, which suggests that when an assignment is built to require genuine engagement, the data reflects it.
  2. Discipline influences editing behavior. STEM students produced more human-generated text than non-STEM students, even though both groups were equally likely to agree with the AI draft’s position on the topic. Subject-matter familiarity alone does not explain the gap. It’s an open question that the researchers have flagged for further study.
  3. Academic standing predicted revision depth. Students who performed above their semester- and major-matched peers revised AI-generated text more extensively. The pattern held across every discipline in the dataset. The tendency to push back on a draft appears to reflect broader academic habits more than discipline-specific knowledge.

On average, students kept about 76% of the AI-generated draft in their final submissions. The roughly 5% who genuinely disagreed with the AI’s position edited far more heavily, which reinforces the assignment’s central logic: Students who have something to say added more of their own writing.

The graph below shows that students with higher academic standing revised AI-generated text more extensively, across every major in the dataset. Each dot represents one student.

Figure reproduced from Harfe & Thomas (2026), “Quantitative Analysis of Generative AI Text Usage and Identification of Factors Influencing Text Choice,” TechTrends. [https://doi.org/10.1007/s11528-026-01182-5] Licensed under CC BY 4.0.

What this means for instructors and institutions

Dr. Harfe’s course is not a template to be copied wholesale. The topic, the student population, and the tool were all choices made in a specific context. But the logic underneath them travels.

Building AI into an assignment rather than designing around it changes the dynamic for students and instructors alike. It is no longer a game of cat and mouse, and instead focuses on the reflection of AI use across the writing process. That’s a more productive conversation, and it’s one that traditional essay design cannot reliably start.

Word-level transparency makes that conversation possible to have with data behind it. Where AI detectors deliver verdicts, Authorship delivers a record. That distinction matters for instructors trying to understand what is happening in their courses and for administrators building AI policies that need to hold up over time.

One of the more persistent worries in higher ed right now is that students will simply hand their thinking over to AI entirely. The data here pushes back on that harder than a usage statistic can. Students in Harfe’s course had explicit, written permission to submit a 100% AI-generated essay and receive full credit. The assignment instructions stated that directly. The only additional requirement was a reflection essay explaining their choices. Despite that, only two of 310 students made no edits to the AI draft. The rest engaged. The students who engaged most deeply were also the strongest academic performers. They did not just happen to engage; they chose to, even though they had every reason not to.

That is worth sitting with. It does not resolve every concern about AI in academic writing, but it does suggest that assignment design has more leverage than most institutions have given it credit for.

“It’s really important to show students what AI can be used for: the good, the bad, the ugly, and then let them make decisions on when and how they should use it in their future lives. Grammarly Authorship is a tool that facilitates that process for faculty in a more collaborative way with students.”

— Dr. Brian Harfe, Professor and Associate Provost, University of Florida

The peer-reviewed study “Quantitative Analysis of Generative AI Text Usage and Identification of Factors Influencing Text Choice” was published in TechTrends in April 2026. Read the full study.

issues.title: Atmos Rewards Summit Visa card review: Stellar value beyond Alaska and Hawaiian
issues.summary: The Atmos Rewards Summit is the premium card for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines flyers, but it holds value for many types of travelers.
issues.author: Augusta Stone
issues.content_html:
The Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card is the premium card for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines loyalists, but look beneath the surface and you'll find a trove of rewards for Oneworld and other flyers, too.

Take it from me: I live in the southeastern U.S. (outside Alaska and Hawaiian's core markets), but I highly value Atmos Rewards points because I can use them to book tickets on American Airlines, the carrier I fly most often, for excellent value. Of course, the Atmos Rewards Summit is a stellar option for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines flyers and those based in the Pacific Northwest as well.

That broad appeal helped the Atmos Summit win TPG's 2026 award for Best New Personal Credit Card. Card rating*: ⭐⭐⭐⭐

*Card rating is based on the opinion of TPG's editors and is not influenced by the card issuer.

Atmos Rewards Summit: The basics

The Atmos Rewards Summit is a cobranded airline card for Atmos Rewards, the joint loyalty program for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. The card earns Atmos Rewards points, which TPG's November 2026 valuations place at 1.6 cents apiece — one of the highest airline currency valuations.

The card charges an annual fee of $395.

Its headline perk is an annual 25,000-point Global Companion Award, but its suite of benefits also includes a free first checked bag and preferred boarding (when you purchase your Alaska or Hawaiian flight with your card).

Cardholders also have a faster path to Atmos Rewards elite status, as they earn 1 status point for every $2 spent (with no spending cap) and receive an anniversary status points boost.

One of my favorite card perks is the Atmos Rewards Summit's standout earning rates, which are especially impressive compared to other airline cobranded cards. Cardholders earn 3 points per dollar spent on all foreign transactions, an unusual (and potentially quite rewarding) bonus category.

One of the best ways to redeem Atmos Rewards points is for flights on Alaska, Hawaiian, Oneworld and other partner airlines.

Related: 10 best ways to redeem 100,000 Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards points

Atmos Rewards Summit pros and cons

ProsCons
  • Annual companion award
  • Fast track to Atmos Rewards elite status
  • Global Entry/TSA PreCheck statement credit
  • High earning rates on international purchases
  • No foreign transaction fees
  • A high annual fee
  • Limited lounge access

Related: Why this is the most rewarding airline card for international travelers

Atmos Rewards Summit benefits

The Atmos Rewards Summit provides multiple benefits when you fly Alaska and Hawaiian, but there are perks to enjoy in other parts of the travel journey as well.

Airline-specific benefits

These benefits kick in when you purchase a fare on Alaska or Hawaiian with your Atmos Rewards Summit:

  • Free checked bag: The cardholder and up to six guests on the same reservation get their first checked bag free.
  • Preferred boarding: The cardholder and up to six guests on the same reservation receive preferred boarding.

The following perks are exclusive to Alaska Airlines flights, though they are expected to eventually be extended to Hawaiian Airlines flights as well:

  • Departure delay voucher: Travelers will receive a $50 voucher if their Alaska Airlines flight is canceled or delayed more than two hours.
  • No change fees: Summit cardholders qualify for same-day confirmed change fee waivers.

Additionally, cardholders can share points with up to 10 other Atmos Rewards members at no additional charge.

Annual companion award

The Atmos Rewards Summit provides an annual 25,000-point Global Companion Award that offers a discount on a second award ticket on Alaska, Hawaiian or a partner airline in any cabin class. This perk is worth $400 per TPG's valuations.

High-spenders who put $60,000 or more on their Atmos Rewards Summit every anniversary year can earn a second 100,000-point Global Companion Award, which TPG values at $1,600. If you already spend a lot on your credit cards, it may be worth re-routing those purchases to your Atmos Summit card.

Elite status boost

  • Anniversary status points: Receive 10,000 status points every card anniversary. This points boost puts you halfway to earning Atmos Rewards Silver status.
  • Faster path to elite status: Earn 1 status point for every $2 spent, with no spending cap. Combined with the anniversary boost, $20,000 in spending earns Atmos Rewards Silver status (which maps to Oneworld Ruby status), and $60,000 earns Gold (equivalent to Oneworld Sapphire).

Related: Atmos Rewards elite status: What it is and how to earn it

Lounge passes

Cardholders receive two Alaska Lounge passes each quarter. These passes can be shared with friends and family.

You must be traveling on a same-day ticketed flight on Alaska, Hawaiian, Oneworld or a partner airline to receive access with your lounge pass. A standard day pass costs $70 per person.

Other benefits

Other key perks include:

  • Two Wi-Fi passes per quarter
  • A $120 Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit every four years
  • Access to Visa Infinite concierge services
  • An auto rental collision damage waiver
  • Extended warranty protection
  • Lost luggage reimbursement
  • No foreign transaction fees
  • Roadside dispatch
  • Travel and emergency assistance services

While these perks certainly help offset the Atmos Rewards Summit's $395 annual fee, this card doesn't offer a full Alaska Lounge membership or the broad collection of lifestyle credits found on some competing premium cards. This could be a downside for cardholders looking for more comprehensive benefits.

However, if you redeem the full 25,000-point Global Companion Award at TPG's valuation, its estimated $400 value slightly exceeds the card's $395 annual fee.

Related: Is the Atmos Rewards Summit worth the annual fee?

How to earn and use Atmos Rewards points

Earning points

Atmos Rewards Summit cardholders earn:

  • 3 points per dollar spent on Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines purchases
  • 3 points per dollar spent on eligible dining and foreign transaction purchases
  • 1 point per dollar spent on all other purchases

Cardholders who have an eligible Bank of America account also earn a 10% rewards bonus on all points earned from card purchases.

The foreign transaction category stands out at 3 points per dollar spent, or an estimated 4.8% return on purchases abroad (5.3% with the Bank of America bonus). The earning rate for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines purchases is standard for an airline cobranded card.

Redeeming points

You'll generally get the most value by using your Atmos points for award flights.

TPG staffer Gabrielle Bernardini recently used her points to snag American Airlines flights from Florida to Philadelphia. With holiday fares being so expensive, redeeming 7,500 points saved her about $200 per person one-way. Plus, since she has the Atmos Summit Card, the $20 per-person partner booking fee was waived.

If an international flight in luxury is more your speed, you can fly from the West Coast to Tokyo in Japan Airlines' business class or to Taipei, Taiwan, in Starlux Airlines' ultramodern business class from 75,000 points. Atmos Rewards allows you to book stopovers and/or multicity award itineraries at no additional cost, so you can combine destinations in one trip.

Related: Beginner's guide to finding award space with ExpertFlyer

Transferring points

The Atmos Rewards Summit offers an unusual benefit for a cobranded airline card: Primary cardholders can transfer Atmos Rewards points to participating hotel programs, which include:

  • IHG One Rewards (1:1 transfer ratio)
  • I Prefer Hotel Rewards (1:2)
  • Marriott Bonvoy (1:1)
  • Shangri-La Circle (8:1)
  • Wyndham Rewards (1:1)

However, you may not want to use your points this way unless you have a specific hotel redemption you're ready to book and need to top off your balance.

Where the Atmos Rewards Summit falls short

The Atmos Rewards Summit may not be the best fit for all types of travelers. Here are some downsides to consider:

  • Most airline benefits are only usable on Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines flights; that could be a deterrent if you aren't frequently flying with these carriers.
  • Lounge passes are limited to two per quarter.
  • You have to pay a high annual fee.
  • Atmos Rewards points have fewer redemption options than transferable credit card rewards.

Atmos Rewards Summit vs. Atmos Rewards Ascent

If you're interested in an Atmos Rewards card but don't want to pay a $395 annual fee for premium perks, I recommend considering the Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card instead.

The Atmos Rewards Ascent charges a $95 annual fee and offers perks similar to those of the Atmos Rewards Summit when flying on Alaska or Hawaiian, including free checked bags and preferred boarding.

Atmos Rewards Ascent cardholders can earn an annual $99 Companion Fare (plus taxes and fees from $23) upon each account anniversary after spending $6,000 or more within the prior anniversary year.

The Atmos Rewards Summit doesn't include this perk, and the two variations aren't direct substitutes. The Ascent's benefit lets you add a companion to an eligible paid Main Cabin itinerary within North America for $99 (plus taxes and fees), while the Summit's award discounts award travel to any destination in any cabin by up to 25,000 points.

To learn more, read our showdown of the Atmos Rewards Ascent versus the Atmos Rewards Summit.

When to apply for the Atmos Rewards Summit

The Atmos Rewards Summit currently offers new cardholders the chance to earn 80,000 bonus points and a 25,000-point Global Companion Award after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening.

Per TPG's valuations, the points and the Global Companion Award included in this bonus are worth $1,680.

We've seen this identical offer come around a few times in the Atmos Rewards Summit's offer history. It's neither the highest or lowest offer the card has, so you'll need to determine if it lines up with when you can meet the spending requirements and have a use in mind for the bonus points and Companion Award.

Since Bank of America issues the Atmos Rewards Summit, you'll most likely be subject to the 2/3/4 rule. This means you can only get approved for two new Bank of America cards in a 30-day period, three cards in 12 months and four cards in two years.

In addition, datapoints suggest Bank of America is inquiry-sensitive, so it may be worth waiting several months from your last hard inquiry before applying. TPG staffers have also found that holding Bank of America checking or savings accounts may increase your odds of approval.

Related: Best welcome offers of this month

Other cards to consider instead of the Atmos Rewards Summit

If the Atmos Rewards Summit isn't the card for you, one of these competitors may be a better fit:

  • If you prefer to earn transferable rewards: The Bilt Palladium Card (see rates and fees) earns Bilt Points that can be transferred to Atmos Rewards. It provides Priority Pass lounge access* and several perks for those ready to dive into Bilt's ecosystem. To learn more, read our full review of the Bilt Palladium.
  • If you're considering another card in the Oneworld alliance: The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees) is the premium airline card that earns AAdvantage miles to redeem with AA, one of Alaska-Hawaiian's Oneworld partners. It provides an Admirals Club membership for those interested in airport lounge access. To learn more, read our full review of the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend.
  • If you own a small business: The Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card is an excellent choice for small-business owners who want to earn Atmos Rewards points. It earns a massive 10 points per dollar spent on flights booked through Atmos for Business and charges a lower $195 annual fee. To learn more, read our full review of the Atmos Rewards Business.

For additional options, see our list of the best airline credit cards.

*A maximum benefit amount and certain restrictions and limitations apply. Please review the Mastercard Guide to Benefits for more details.

Related: Why I'm considering a Citi credit card as an Alaska Airlines fan

Bottom line

The Atmos Rewards Summit provides fantastic value for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines flyers ready to go all in on their joint loyalty program. The card's 25,000-point Global Companion Award, Alaska Lounge passes and high earning rate on foreign transactions are top-notch perks.

However, if you're more of a casual traveler and aren't chasing Atmos Rewards elite status, you may be better off with the mid-tier Atmos Rewards Ascent.

Overall, Atmos Rewards points are a standout currency that can unlock redemptions across the Oneworld alliance, so the Atmos Rewards Summit is worth a look regardless of where you're flying from.

Apply here: Atmos Rewards Summit Visa Infinite credit card

issues.title: The 5 best cruise lines for families
issues.summary: Royal Caribbean, Disney Cruise Line and Norwegian Cruise Line are among our favorite brands for families. Here's why.
issues.author: Erica Silverstein
issues.content_html:
The best cruise lines for families allow parents and kids to have fun together and apart while taking the stress out of group travel.

Our favorite family ships mix wow-factor activities with attractive kids clubs, plentiful and convenient dining and thoughtful touches like bathtubs and babysitting.

Your family might be happy anywhere there's a beach or pool, but if you want an at-sea family vacation you'll always remember, book a sailing with one of our top five cruise lines for families.

Disney Cruise Line

No one will be surprised that entertainment juggernaut Disney offers an amazing family cruise experience.

Disney Cruise Line ships are known for meet-and-greets with Mickey Mouse and Disney princesses, interactive movie-themed dining experiences and enormous kids clubs and play areas.

What might surprise the uninitiated is how good the line is at taking care of the whole family, not just the Mouse-obsessed little ones.

Disney thinks of all the little things that can help parents have a stress-free trip with kids in tow. From split bathrooms (allowing one family member to take a bath while another uses the toilet) to waiters who will cut up your child's food, Disney Cruise Line takes the pressure off parents.

While other cruise lines limit water play to kids who are toilet trained and drop-off child care to ages 3 and up, Disney caters to all kids with onboard splash areas and nurseries for kids ages 6 months to 3 years.

Kids ages 3 to 10 live it up in the expansive Oceaneer Club, with attractions like an interactive replica of Star Wars' Millennium Falcon and a play area designed to look like Andy's Room from "Toy Story."

Teens might roll their eyes at the ever-present Mickeys, but Disney Cruise Line does not ignore its older kid guests. Tweens and teens get their own cool hangouts, Edge (ages 11 to 14) and Vibe (ages 14 to 17), with video games, foosball and seating areas.

Additionally, first-run movies and Broadway-caliber musicals, waterslides, teen spa treatments and grab-and-go food options (and free room service) keep older kids busy and happy.

Sister ships Disney Wish, Disney Treasure and Disney Destiny feature Hero Zone sports areas for free play and competitions attractive to this age group. (Keep an eye out for the Disney Believe, too, debuting in late 2027.)

Grownups on Disney get to play as hard as they parent. Ships offer adults-only pool decks and restaurants, a nightlife scene and couples spa treatments to revive exhausted parents who haven't had a date in months.

The only caveat is that Disney Cruise Line is the most expensive cruise line on this list. At press time, seven-night Caribbean cruises start at $3,180 per person.

Related: These are the best cruise ships for kids

Royal Caribbean

With some of the biggest ships at sea and an amusement park-like private island in the Bahamas, Royal Caribbean is one of the best cruise lines for active families.

Want to try surfing, sky diving, rock climbing, laser tag, bumper cars or zip lining? Families don't have to leave the ship to find their adrenaline highs.

Even the sedentary pursuits are high-octane on Royal Caribbean. Broadway musicals, festive parades, water acrobatic performances and ice skating shows wow the crowds in the evenings and on sea days.

Expansive play spaces for kids includedrop-off nurseries for babies (ages 6 to 36 months) and Adventure Ocean for kids ages 3 to 12 (often broken into separate activities for kids ages 3 to 5, 6 to 8, and 9 to 12) with science labs and art studios on the biggest ships. Teens and tweens ages 13 to 17 get their own cool hangouts, often with activities scheduled around the ship.

While the kids live it up at cruise camp, parents can sneak off to the adults-only solarium or thermal suite.

After a hard day of play, worn-out families can refuel at a variety of restaurants, including burger and milkshake mecca Johnny Rockets, Italian and Mexican eateries and an all-day buffet.

Family cabins and connecting staterooms give larger families their needed space. The Ultimate Family Suite (and similar Ultimate Family Townhouses on some of the line's biggest ships) can sleep eight to 10 people, and parents and kids alike might be tempted to stay up late playing air hockey, scrambling up the climbing wall, soaking in the private outdoor hot tub or watching the giant TV.

Royal Caribbean's biggest ships – Icon, Star, and Legend of the Seas – also offers an entire section of the ship devoted to family-friendly accommodations and an outdoor dining-and-play space targeted at parents with young children.

Families should keep an eye out for kids-sail-free deals on select departures, which allow kids ages 12 and younger to pay no cruise fare when they sail as the third or fourth guest in a cabin with two full-fare-paying adults. (Note that families will still have to pay taxes, fees and port charges for kids sailing free.)

Fares for Royal Caribbean cruises can vary based on ship, and its newest, biggest ships often command premium pricing. Seven-night Caribbean cruises start from $444 per person on an older ship, but cost more than $1,000 per person on its biggest Icon Class ships.

Related: These are the best cruises for teens

Carnival Cruise Line

Practicalities first: Carnival Cruise Line is an affordable and convenient cruise line for families who don't live the jet-set lifestyle. With home ports all around the U.S., Carnival puts its ships within driving distance of many Americans.

A variety of short-cruise destinations, affordable-yet-spacious inside cabins (some that sleep up to four people) and lots of onboard attractions and restaurants included in the fares combine to make it one of the best value cruise lines afloat.

Carnival doesn't dub its fleet the Fun Ships for nothing. The whole family will have a blast on board, whether you like getting down to live music, busting a gut at family-friendly comedy shows, being soaked at an onboard water park or eating green eggs and ham with Dr. Seuss characters.

The cruise line also embraces simple pleasures like free-flowing soft-serve ice cream and pizza and a day spent lounging by the pool.

Families don't need to pull out their wallets to feed ravenous teens or sugar-fueled children. Guy Fieri burgers and barbecue, burritos for breakfast and lunch and Shaquille O'Neal's fried chicken are all included in your cruise fares. No one's going to make you dress up for dinner, either.

Carnival ships have plenty of cabins that can sleep four or five passengers, but six of its newerst ships truly treat families right. Book a Family Harbor cabin or suite on Vista or Excel Class ships and get access to a family lounge stocked with all the essentials — snacks and coffee, games, Wi-Fi, movies and a concierge to make bookings so mom and dad can spend more time playing with the kids.

Seven-night Caribbean cruises start at $443 per person.

MSC Cruises

It might not be a household name yet, but any cruise line that has a partnership with Lego should be on every family's radar, so MSC Cruises is a line families should know.

As the Mediterranean line grows its U.S.-based fleet, it's adding newer and bigger family-friendly ships to more home ports, including Miami, Port Canaveral, Galveston and Seattle.

MSC World America, the line's newest and biggest ship sailing the Caribbean, features the Family Aventura district, a hub for kids and their grownups. It features The Harbour, an outdoor space with a ropes course, waterpark, playground and 11-deck-long dry slide; indoor sports area for family games and bumper cars; and an enormous Doremiland kids club.

Speaking of kids clubs, MSC's ships offer play spaces for babies, kids, tweens and teens. Its ships not only offer a drop-off Baby Club (ages 6 months to 3 years) with educational toys by Chicco but also a special baby laundry service to take care of that pile of dirty onesies.

MSC divides young cruisers into Mini Club (ages 3 to 6), Junior Club (ages 7 to 11) and Young Club (12 to 14). Kids club activities go beyond arts and crafts and video games to include cooking events, sports competitions and high-tech interactive games. Teens (ages 15 to 17) can sing karaoke, dance at the onboard disco and attend themed parties with their new friends.

Outside of the kids club, families can race in a Formula One simulator, experience virtual reality, be soaked in a water park or brave their fear of heights on a suspension bridge.

Several MSC Cruises ships offer thrill rides that will appeal to all ages of adventurous cruisers. MSC Seascape features Robotron, a three-seat robotic amusement ride and MSC World America and MSC World Atlantic (coming late 2027) have the Cliffhanger, an overwater swing ride – both are hits with thrill-seeking families.

Multigenerational groups can choose connecting cabins for more space, but families keen on rooming together can take advantage of frequent "kids sail free" fares and pay only the taxes and fees for children under 18 who are the third and fourth passengers in a cabin. Seven-night Caribbean cruises start from $299 per person.

Norwegian Cruise Line

Norwegian Cruise Line is all about giving cruisers options to create different versions of the perfect cruise vacation, all within the same ship.

The flexibility and choice make it one of the best cruise lines for families, especially those who need to satisfy diverse interests or who are easily bored with the same activities day after day.

Kids clubs and adults-only sundecks allow for age-appropriate fun time apart, but Norwegian wants families to have fun together. Its Splash Academy engages kids ages 3 to 12 with group activities like team challenges and crafts, while Entourage is the place for teens ages 13 to 17 to make friends, hang out playing foosball and video games or show off their moves during evening dance parties. Adults can hide out in the 18+ Vibe Beach Club and Spice H2O for some sunbathing and hot tub time while the kids are engaged in youth activities.

Norwegian also wants families to have fun together. Teaming up to solve a murder mystery, mastering a ropes course, singing along to a high-energy musical show or live concert or screaming down a waterslide are guaranteed to create those unbreakable family bonds.

Norwegian's flexible dining system and a plethora of onboard eateries let families plan meals to suit their schedules and tastes.

Also, free kids meals at extra-charge restaurants mean parents can sample Brazilian, Japanese, French or seafood dishes while the littles gobble up pasta and chicken fingers. Casual all-day options suit fussy eaters who need unfussy dining areas.

The cruise line also gets a shoutout for its family-friendly Hawaii itineraries. As the only big-ship cruise line that sails weeklong itineraries round trip from Honolulu, Norwegian provides an easy way for families to visit multiple islands.

Beach time, boat rides, water sports, luaus and volcano tours combine for an epic family trip, with the ship taking the stress out of meals and transportation.

In the Bahamas, Norwegian's enhanced Great Stirrup Cay private island now features a waterpark with a variety of slides, a cliff jump and a not-that-lazy river (entrance fee required), as well as free use of a giant pool and a splash playground for little kids, making beach days even more fun for vacationing families.

To make it all more affordable, families should keep an eye on Norwegian's Free at Sea promotion, which sometimes includes free third and fourth guest fares. That means that kids sharing a room with two paying adults sail free. Fares for seven-night Caribbean cruises start at $399 per person.

Bottom line

Families can have a great time on almost any cruise line, hanging out by the pool, visiting exciting new destinations and simply spending time together. But if you're looking for a ship that really caters to kids and their adult companions, you'll want to book a vacation with one of these five best cruise lines for families.

issues.title: United partner TAP adding a 2nd Portugal route from Washington, DC
issues.summary: TAP will link Washington, D.C., with Porto in Portugal next summer.
issues.author: Edward Russell
issues.content_html:
Washingtonians have a new option to Portugal next summer.

TAP Air Portugal will launch a new thrice-weekly service from Dulles International Airport (IAD) to Porto Airport (OPO) on March 30, 2027. Westbound flights will operate on Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays through the summer, and on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays beginning in October.

TAP, a Star Alliance partner of United Airlines, will fly an Airbus A321LR on the new IAD-OPO route. The long-range, single-aisle aircraft is fitted with 16 lie-flat business-class seats and 155 economy seats.

The new Portugal route is the latest international addition at IAD. United plans to launch new service to Toulouse, France, in April and to Milan in May, using its new long-range A321XLR on the former route.

International seats from IAD will increase nearly 7% in the first six months of 2027 compared to this year, schedule data from aviation analytics firm Cirium shows.

IAD is undergoing a massive, $22 billion redevelopment to bring its infrastructure up to modern standards. The first piece — a 14-gate section of the new Concourse E that includes a new, large United Club — opened earlier in November. Future phases include a new international arrivals facility that would support additional long-haul growth.

And if the redevelopment plan stays on schedule, IAD could retire its jet-age mobile lounges by the mid-2030s.

TAP's new OPO route complements its existing service to IAD from Lisbon Airport (LIS).

The state-owned Portuguese airline is in the process of being privatized as part of the Lufthansa Group. The German airline conglomerate plans to buy an initial 44.9% stake in TAP, aiming to close the deal by the first quarter of 2028.

Lufthansa Group chief commercial officer Dieter Vranckx said in October that once the TAP deal is done, Lufthansa intends to integrate the Portuguese airline into its transatlantic joint venture with Air Canada and United.

issues.title: Citi Shop offers an easier way to save when shopping online
issues.summary: Citi Shop offers statement credits and coupon codes at thousands of retailers. Learn how it works, when to use it and how it compares with shopping portals.
issues.author: Becky Pokora
issues.content_html:
Citi Shop takes some of the work out of saving money online. Once you've installed its browser extension, it acts as a shopping portal and coupon hunter all-in-one, rewarding you with statement credits.

It has broad reach, too, with more than 5,000 participating online merchants. That's easier than a traditional online shopping portal, which requires you to remember to start at the portal and click through before filling your cart.

Its ease of use makes it a great resource, but other portals or special discounts may save you more.

Here's how Citi Shop works and what to consider to determine if it's the best savings path for you.

What is Citi Shop?

Citi Shop is a free browser extension for primary cardholders with an eligible Citi credit card, including ThankYou points cards and cobranded cards. Citi retail and commercial cards are usually ineligible.

Offers come as either a percentage back or a fixed amount back, and your earnings are applied as a statement credit on the Citi card you selected during enrollment.

Citi Shop is separate from Citi Merchant Offers, which requires you to enroll in targeted offers with a specific Citi card and then use that card for the qualifying purchase.

How Citi Shop differs from online shopping portals

Both Citi Shop and traditional portals give you an extra reward for making purchases they track.

But Citi Shop brings potential rebates to you, rather than requiring you to initiate your savings search. The extension automatically displays a pop-up with an available offer when you visit a participating website. You'll have the option to activate the offer before checkout.

All of Citi Shop's rebates are provided as statement credits, unlike the potential airline miles, hotel points or credit card rewards of traditional portals.

What I like about Citi Shop is that it also acts like a shopping assistant. Instead of opening six coupon sites only to discover that every code expired last Tuesday, it handles the scavenger hunt for you and tests available promo codes on your behalf.

Like Capital One Shopping, Citi Shop uses a browser extension. However, Capital One Shopping doesn't require a Capital One card to enroll and its rewards can be redeemed for eligible gift cards instead of a statement credit.

Generally speaking, Citi Shop clashes with other shopping portals. Both work by referring and tracking your purchase, so they can be mutually exclusive. You'll need to make your purchase through whichever offer is better.

Related: Chase shopping portal guide: How to earn bonus Ultimate Rewards points

How to use Citi Shop

  1. Install the extension from citi.com/citishopenroll (available on supported desktop browsers and iOS devices, but not Android).
  2. Choose which Citi card you prefer to enroll.
  3. Shop online as usual.
  4. Activate in your browser pop-up before checkout.
  5. Let Citi Shop test coupons.
  6. Track pending and paid credits on your Citi Shop dashboard.

Unless Citi Shop finds a promo code, it won't lower your total at checkout. Its returns arrive later as statement credits and may require patiently waiting two to six months, sometimes longer.

What credit card should you use with Citi Shop?

Even though you need an eligible Citi card to enroll, you don't have to pay with it. Citi allows any payment method accepted by the merchant.

I really appreciate the flexibility to choose the best card for each purchase. For electronics, I might pick a card with an extended warranty while I might stick to a travel rewards credit card for hotel bookings. You can even pay with a gift card if you wish.

Regardless of how you pay, the statement credit will post to the Citi card you enrolled.

How to maximize Citi Shop

If you have an eligible Citi card but rarely remember to click through a shopping portal, Citi Shop is an easy win. Install it, activate offers when the pop-up appears and let the credits come to you. That convenience can also be a big benefit if you have partners or other family members who aren't as motivated to strategize on rewards as you are.

But with a little extra effort, you might be able to earn even more. When the Citi Shop pop-up appears with an offer, take a minute to compare before you click Activate.

Checking a shopping portal aggregator such as Cashback Monitor shows payouts from multiple cash-back, airline and credit card portals, making it easier to compare a Citi Shop statement credit with points or miles elsewhere.

Then layer more savings:

  • A retailer's sale price
  • A coupon found or permitted by Citi Shop
  • The Citi Shop statement credit
  • Rewards from the credit card used to pay
  • A card-linked offer, such as Citi Merchant Offers

Suppose a $200 jacket is marked down to $160. Citi Shop finds a $10 coupon, bringing the checkout price to $150, and offers 8% back. Assuming the full amount qualifies, you'd receive a $12 Citi Shop credit. If you pay with a card that earns 2% back and has an activated merchant offer for $5 off a $100 purchase, you'd collect another $8. After all the credits and rewards post, your net cost would be $130.

Read the terms before getting too excited. Some brands, products, gift cards or coupon codes may be excluded and you might not be able to stack every layer every time. Still, you can often use multiple discounts simultaneously for a better deal.

When do Citi Shop statement credits post?

Citi Shop is not a program for instant gratification. Citi says statement credits post 61 to 180 days after a completed purchase, though some can take longer.

In many cases, offers may show as pending long before they officially pay out, to account for potential returns. Hotel rewards may remain pending until after the stay. Eventually, you'll see it on your statement as "CITI SHOP STATEMENT CREDIT."

If a credit hasn't posted after the expected window, contact Citi using the number on the back of your enrolled card. You may want to keep good records along the way, like a screenshot of the offer and an e-receipt from the purchase.

Bottom line

Citi Shop's biggest advantage is convenience. It does the heavy lifting by reminding you to activate offers so you don't miss out on earnings from your online orders, while testing coupon codes along the way. The offers themselves may or may not be the highest available, but they are certainly the easiest.

To truly optimize your returns, you'll want to compare Citi Shop earnings with those from other shopping portals — and stack other forms of saving along the way. But when that sounds like too much, the ease of this extension can still be a great way to tack on some extra returns.

issues.summary: One of the most extraordinary attractions in northern Norway is Alta Museum's outdoor area, where thousands of prehistoric carvings can be found. issues.content_html:
One of the most extraordinary attractions in northern Norway is Alta Museum's outdoor area, where thousands of prehistoric carvings can be found. These are not paintings or replicas displayed behind glass – they are original artworks carved directly into the bedrock by people thousands of years ago.

Some of the carvings date back more than 7,000 years, making them among the oldest and most significant examples of prehistoric rock art in Northern Europe. They depict reindeer, bears, elk, fish, whales, boats, hunting scenes, fishing activities, human figures and mysterious rituals. The carvings were originally made near the shoreline, and as the land gradually rose after the last Ice Age, new rock surfaces became available for successive generations of artists.

Light plays an important role in discovering the carvings. Depending on the direction and angle of the sunlight, the engraved lines can become much more visible or almost disappear completely. Low-angle sunlight, especially in the morning or evening, creates small shadows inside the carved grooves, making the figures stand out more clearly.

Some of the carvings have been painted red to make them easier to see. This red colour is not original to the carvings, but was added in 1970s to help visitors recognise their shapes and details. Today, the focus is on protecting the original rock carvings while keeping modern alterations to a minimum. As part of this conservation work, the red paint is gradually being removed to preserve the site's authenticity

The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognised in 1985 for its outstanding cultural and historical importance.

issues.content_html:
Rather than being an impressive, polished wax museum, the Visulahti Wax Museum has become famous for its awkward, outdated, and sometimes unintentionally hilarious figures.

The museum has something of a cult reputation in Finland. Its wax figures are famously questionable in quality: many look surprisingly inaccurate, while some remind you more of a horror movie setting. In 1983, the Wax Museum was established with serious intentions, but nowadays people visit it mainly for nostalgic reasons. You have to approach the museum with a good sense of humour.

The collection rarely gets updated, and the once-popular TV stars are now unfamiliar to the younger audience. The newest figurine is the Finnish president, whose resemblance – or the lack of it – has been widely discussed in the national news.

There are also international stars displayed at the museum, such as Elvis, the Beatles, and Santa Claus. At the end of the tour, a creepy version of Mickey Mouse sings to you with his friends, as you walk out of the building, wondering what you just experienced.
